doc.title: Will Shade and Dewey Corley Interview, 1960-05-25

title: Frank Stokes's son, Dan Sane and James Dewberry
summary: Corley mentions Roosevelt Stokes and Earl Bell, Frank Stokes's guitar playing, Dan Sane, and one-legged guitarist James Dewberry in St. Louis.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: I see. Well, we've got to get back to Dewey now. Yeah, I think we're about to run out. Unless Dewey wants to tell us some more of his favorite musicians.
Well, I don't know that many of them. I used to play around with a boy called Frank Stokes. The old man, he's dead. That is his son.

His son named Roosevelt Stokes. Another boy called Earl Bell. See, all those guys. They real young. They young than we are. See, they didn't know anything. And not to do no good. They liked from under the bus.
What was Frank Stokes like? Did he play good?
Dan Sane. I know of him.

Yeah. I don't know why he's at, but he's around here someplace. And James Dewberry. He's a one-legged boy. He's in St. Louis. I've got his address in my pocket. He plays good guitar. He's like right off and under me and son of the room. Yeah, well shaved, you might call it.

He's a good guitar player. He made a couple of records too here a long time ago. I've got his address now, but I ain't seen him in about, oh, three or four, four, five years or longer. Because here about four or five months ago he comes through here.
